pregame.whyWatch: Division game: Cardinals 1-3, 4th in the NFC West; Rams 2-2, 3rd in the NFC West.
pregame.pressurePoint: Cardinals pass game vs Rams pass defense. The Rams are No. 11 of 32 at limiting explosive passes (1.27) and No. 3 in pass success allowed (40%). The Cardinals rank No. 32 in pass explosiveness (1.01) and No. 18 in pass success rate (46%). This is not a lean. It is a mismatch, and a prominent one. Deep balls are the lowest-percentage play in this game. The Cardinals need the underneath game and yards after catch. Watch the longest Cardinals completion. If it is under 25 yards at the half, the Rams have won the matchup.

edges.why: The Rams are No. 11 of 32 at limiting explosive passes (1.27) and No. 3 in pass success allowed (40%). The Cardinals rank No. 32 in pass explosiveness (1.01) and No. 18 in pass success rate (46%). This is not a lean. It is a mismatch, and a prominent one. Deep balls are the lowest-percentage play in this game. The Cardinals need the underneath game and yards after catch.

The Rams are No. 19 of 32 in pass explosiveness (1.30) and No. 13 in pass success rate (47%). The Cardinals rank No. 32 at limiting explosive passes (1.68) and No. 21 in pass success allowed (47%). A clear edge, the kind that shapes a game plan. The Rams have the deep ball available. Watch whether the Cardinals roll a safety over after the first one.

The Rams are No. 23 in passing-downs success (32%), and the Cardinals are No. 19 on passing downs (38%). Strength on strength. Both sides are average on long downs. Early-down efficiency decides who sees more of them.

The Cardinals are No. 7 in rush success rate (46%) and No. 14 in EPA a carry (-0.03), and the Rams are No. 9 against the run (37%) and No. 8 by EPA a carry (-0.11). Strength on strength. Neither side has shown it can impose the run on a unit this good. The first stuffed series tells you who blinks.
